The product's microphone and surround-sound settings [appears|appear|'The microphone and settings' is plural, so use 'appear'.] beside the price. The campaign presents the disabled player as a decision maker within the group, not as an inspirational exception.

title: Premium noise-cancelling headphones
text: A transit poster for premium noise-cancelling headphones shows a woman sitting in a busy station with a notebook open on her lap. The crowd around her is [render|rendered|After 'is', use the past participle for the passive: is rendered.] as blurred streaks, but a friend beside her remains [sharp|sharply|Use the adverb 'sharply' before 'visible'.] visible. “Choose what comes through” appears above a small explanation of the listening modes. A QR code leads to a demonstration and the high price. The composition suggests that concentration need not mean withdrawing from people altogether, while the spotless headphones [stands|stand|'The spotless headphones' is plural, so use 'stand'.] out against the [stations|station's|Add 's to show that the realism belongs to the station.] untidy realism.

title: Family tablet
text: An online video for a family tablet begins with a grandmother teaching two children a card game. When the rules [becomes|become|'The rules' is plural, so use 'become'.] complicated, the [oldest|older|There are two children, so use the comparative: older.] child records her explanation on the tablet; later, they use it to call a cousin who [live|lives|'Who' refers to one cousin, so use 'lives'.] abroad. The screen remains visible without replacing the cards or the conversation. “Keep the good bits going” appears beside the model and price. The grandmother supplies the knowledge, while the children help with the technology, so expertise [move|moves|'Expertise' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: moves.] in both directions across the generations.

title: Professional camera
text: In an online video for a professional camera, a photographer takes portraits of workers at a night market. He asks a [cooks|cook's|Add 's to show that the permission belongs to the cook.] permission before [photograph|photographing|After 'before', use the -ing form: before photographing.] her, then shows her the image on the camera screen. The cook suggests a different angle that [include|includes|'A different angle' is singular, so add -s.] the whole stall. Close-ups demonstrate the camera's controls in low light; a final card links to technical specifications and the premium price. The small exchange gives the person being photographed some authority over how she is represented, rather than treating her [simple|simply|Use the adverb 'simply' before 'as an interesting face'.] as an interesting face.

title: Fitness tracker
text: This television advert for a fitness tracker follows three people through an ordinary [tuesday|Tuesday|Days of the week take a capital letter: Tuesday.]. A delivery rider checks the distance travelled, an office worker takes a short walk at lunch, and an older woman records a gentle exercise class. Their numbers [differs|differ|'Their numbers' is plural, so use 'differ'.], and none is described as a winner. The voiceover says, “Measure your day on your terms,” while the screen shows the tracker and its health settings. The closing price [include|includes|'The closing price' is singular, so add -s.] a note about optional paid features. The advert values varied routines, though every activity is still [convert|converted|After 'is', use the past participle for the passive: is converted.] into data.

title: Home security system
text: A sponsored social post for a home security system shows a couple returning from a weekend away. Their door camera has recorded a neighbour watering the plants and a parcel being [leave|left|After 'being', use the past participle: being left.] safely. The caption explains how alerts can be [share|shared|After 'can be', use the past participle: can be shared.] with trusted people, while a short clip shows one partner setting the system up. Both [participates|participate|'Both' is plural, so use 'participate'.] in the decisions. A clearly marked “Ad” label, installation cost and monthly fee [appears|appear|'A label, installation cost and monthly fee' is plural, so use 'appear'.] beneath the video. The story sells a sense of community as well as technology, despite depending on constant recording.

title: Entry-level laptop
text: A billboard for an entry-level laptop shows a young man at a library table, helping his mother complete an online course. Beside them, another student [use|uses|'Another student' is one person, so add -s.] the same model to edit a presentation. “Good work starts somewhere” sits above the price in [unusual|unusually|Use the adverb 'unusually' before 'large'.] large type. A QR code leads to a list of the [laptops|laptop's|Add 's to show that the specifications belong to the laptop.] specifications and repair options. The advert makes adult learning [visibly|visible|After 'makes adult learning', use the adjective: visible.] and treats the son as a collaborator rather than a digital rescuer. The public library setting gives the affordable device a credible everyday context.

title: Family car
text: In a sponsored social post for a family car, a parent describes the weekly journey between two homes after a separation. The video shows a father collecting his daughter, making space for her music case and [ask|asking|Keep the list parallel: collecting, making and asking.] which route she [prefer|prefers|'She' takes a verb with -s: prefers.]. The mother waves from the door; she is part of the family without being inside the car. A caption lists the [vehicles|vehicle's|Add 's to show that the safety features belong to the vehicle.] safety features, price and finance terms. The small story broadens the usual image of family travel, while the sponsor label keeps [it's|its|'It's' means 'it is'. 'Its' shows belonging: its commercial purpose.] commercial purpose visible.

title: Luxury car
text: A transit poster for a luxury car shows a [sharp|sharply|Use the adverb 'sharply' before 'dressed'.] dressed woman seated in the back, revising notes before a public speech. The driver is visible only through a reflection in the window. “Arrive ready” appears beside the car's name in silver lettering; neither a price nor a practical specification is [provide|provided|After 'is', use the past participle for the passive: is provided.]. Her professional responsibility makes her more than a passive passenger, but the blurred driver [illustrate|illustrates|'The blurred driver' is singular, so add -s.] whose labour the image chooses to overlook. The poster invites commuters to identify with the calm, [priviledged|privileged|Spell 'privileged' with no d before the g.] person being transported.

title: City bicycle
text: This magazine advert for a city bicycle shows an older man cycling past shops that [has|have|'Shops' is plural, so use 'have'.] known him for decades. He stops to collect bread, checks his lights and [greet|greets|'He' takes a verb with -s: greets.] a young neighbour riding to school. The headline, “Your city is still yours,” sits above a map of local cycle routes. A smaller panel gives the bike's price, weight and step-through frame details. His age is presented through his relationships and [knowlege|knowledge|Spell 'knowledge' with -dge.] of the neighbourhood rather than through a claim that the bicycle will make him [feeling|feel|After 'make him', use the base verb: feel.] young again.

title: Racing bicycle
text: An online video for a racing bicycle follows a woman returning to training after an injury. She adjusts the bike with her coach, rides a short stretch and stops when her leg [begin|begins|'Her leg' is singular, so add -s.] to hurt. Later scenes show [gradually|gradual|Before a noun, use an adjective: gradual improvement.] improvement, not an instant race victory. Technical captions explain the frame's fit and weight, followed by its high price. Her decisions about recovery [carries|carry|'Her decisions' is plural, so use 'carry'.] the story; the bike supports her work without pretending to remove its difficulty. The coach is [credit|credited|After 'is', use the past participle for the passive: is credited.] on screen, an unusual detail in a performance-focused campaign.

title: Budget hotel stay
text: A billboard for a budget hotel stay shows two friends eating takeaway food on the bed after a day [explore|exploring|After 'a day', use the -ing form: a day exploring.] a new city. Their shoes and maps are [scatter|scattered|After 'are', use the past participle for the passive: are scattered.] around a small but tidy room. “Save on the room. Stay for the trip” appears beside the nightly price. The hotel name, location and booking QR code [is|are|'The name, location and code' is plural, so use 'are'.] easy to read from a bus stop. The image treats a limited budget as a [sensitive|sensible|'Sensitive' means easily upset. A wise choice is 'sensible'.] travel choice, although it shows none of the staff who clean and prepare the room.

title: Luxury hotel stay
text: In a podcast advert for a luxury hotel, a travel writer describes waking before sunrise to hear the harbour. A concierge then speaks about arranging a boat trip, and a chef explains one breakfast dish. Their names are given, but the writer [recieves|receives|I before e except after c: receives.] the longest speaking time. Soft music and the sound of waves [creates|create|'Soft music and the sound of waves' is plural, so use 'create'.] a private, unhurried atmosphere. The host names the hotel's [sweets|suites|'Sweets' are sugary food. Sets of hotel rooms are 'suites'.] and booking link without stating a price. The advert makes service central to the experience while [careful|carefully|Use the adverb 'carefully' before 'controlling'.] controlling how much the workers can say.

title: Household vacuum cleaner
text: An online video for a household vacuum cleaner shows a shared apartment preparing for a party. Three flatmates divide the jobs: one [tidys|tidies|Change y to -ies: tidies.] books, another cooks, and the third uses the vacuum on a rug. When a guest [arrive|arrives|'A guest' is singular, so add -s.] early, they finish together. A product close-up shows the attachments, and a caption gives the price and warranty. None of the flatmates is made the [permanant|permanent|Spell 'permanent' with -ent.] cleaner. The advert presents a functional machine within an imperfect home, where tidiness is something people create together before [welcome|welcoming|After 'before', use the -ing form: before welcoming.] friends.

title: Premium robot vacuum
text: In a podcast advert for a premium robot vacuum, a novelist describes the noise of her apartment settling after her children [leaves|leave|'Her children' is plural, so use 'leave'.] for school. She starts the vacuum through an app, then reads her draft aloud while it works. Her partner calls to ask about dinner, and they agree to share the cooking. The host explains scheduling, the high price and [maintainance|maintenance|Spell 'maintenance' with -ten- in the middle.] needs. The story sells [a|an|Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an extra hour.] extra hour for creative work, although the machine can only perform one part of the household labour that usually [interrupt|interrupts|'The household labour' is singular, so add -s.] it.

title: Flat-pack sofa
text: A website banner for a flat-pack sofa presents a sequence of photographs [took|taken|Use the past participle after 'photographs': photographs taken.] in the same small living room. Two friends assemble the sofa, a neighbour helps carry away the boxes, and a child later [turn|turns|'A child' is singular, so add -s.] the cushions into a fort. “Made for life after the instructions” appears above the price and delivery options. Clicking [open|opens|The subject 'clicking' is singular, so use 'opens'.] a genuine assembly guide. The people and room are slightly untidy, giving the furniture a lived-in setting. The neighbour is more [then|than|'Then' is about time. Use 'than' to compare.] a convenient extra pair of hands: she joins the final gathering.

title: Designer sofa
text: A podcast advert for a designer sofa is [build|built|After 'is', use the past participle for the passive: is built.] around a conversation between a furniture maker and a woman choosing a seat for her mother. They discuss fabric, support and how her mother likes to read by the window. The mother then joins the conversation and [firm|firmly|Use the adverb 'firmly' to say how she rejects it.] rejects the first colour. The maker explains the materials, followed by a consultation link and no stated price. Her voice prevents the older woman from [become|becoming|After 'prevent someone from', use the -ing form.] merely a reason for someone else's purchase, while the bespoke service [signal|signals|'The bespoke service' is singular, so add -s.] a wealthy audience.

title: Shampoo
text: In a podcast advert for shampoo, a teenage swimmer describes the smell of the pool and the long journey home after training. Her father asks about her race while she washes her hair; she talks more about her teammates [then|than|'Then' is about time. Use 'than' to compare.] her time. A narrator briefly names the [shampoos|shampoo's|Add 's to show that the formula belongs to the shampoo.] gentle formula, price and shop availability. Splashes and muffled conversation make the scene [vividly|vivid|After 'make the scene', use the adjective: vivid.] without requiring any visual promise of perfect hair. The swimmer's sport and friendships [defines|define|'The swimmer's sport and friendships' is plural, so use 'define'.] her, while the product occupies a practical moment in her routine.

title: Premium skincare serum
text: A sponsored social post for premium skincare serum features a woman in her sixties explaining how she cares for her skin before working outdoors in her garden. She names the serum, then [remembers|reminds|You 'remember' something yourself. To make other people remember is to 'remind' them.] viewers that she also wears a hat and sunscreen. The caption lists the ingredients, price and sponsored partnership. Natural light leaves wrinkles visible, and her gardening knowledge [fill|fills|'Her gardening knowledge' is singular, so add -s.] more of the video than the product demonstration. The campaign offers an expensive routine without [inferring|implying|The viewer 'infers'. The advert 'implies'.] that age itself is a [floor|flaw|A 'floor' is what you stand on. A fault is a 'flaw'.] to be corrected.

title: Mobile data plan
text: This transit poster for a mobile data plan depicts two brothers exchanging photographs of a family celebration. One is travelling by train; the other is helping their father set up the tables at home. The headline says, “Still in the room,” beside a [plain|plainly|Use the adverb 'plainly' before 'stated'.] stated monthly [allowence|allowance|Spell 'allowance' with -ance.] and price. Small print explains the speed after the allowance is used. The family appears connected across distance, although the poster's central image of the smiling traveller [make|makes|'The poster's central image' is singular, so add -s.] the brother doing the practical preparation less [noticable|noticeable|Keep the e: notice + able = noticeable.] at first glance.

title: Private tutoring service
text: A magazine advert for private tutoring shows a girl correcting her own essay with a tutor sitting beside her. Several [draughts|drafts|'Draughts' are cold air or a board game. Versions of an essay are 'drafts'.] are spread over the table, and a handwritten note says, “This sentence says what I mean.” The headline, “The answer should sound like you,” links tutoring with confidence rather than a guaranteed grade. Qualifications, session format and a high hourly rate [appears|appear|'Qualifications, format and rate' is plural, so use 'appear'.] in a side panel. The girl's revision work is visible, but the calm private study and price also [reveals|reveal|'The calm private study and price' is plural, so use 'reveal'.] which families can most [ready|readily|Use the adverb 'readily' before 'purchase'.] purchase this help.

title: Gym membership
text: This television advert for a gym membership opens with a crowded beginner's class in which the instructor [demonstrate|demonstrates|'The instructor' is one person, so add -s.] easier and harder versions of the same movement. Participants choose their own pace, including a young man who [pause|pauses|'Who' refers to one young man, so use 'pauses'.] and an older woman who continues. The music fades as the instructor says, “You can come back tomorrow.” The final screen lists facilities, access information and the monthly price. The advert presents fitness as repeated participation rather than a dramatic transformation, although the camera still [favour|favours|'The camera' is singular, so add -s.] the [more|most|Comparing all the members, use the superlative: most energetic.] energetic members.

title: Wellness retreat
text: In a magazine advert for a wellness retreat, two friends sit silently on a path above a forest. One [wear|wears|'One' is singular, so use 'wears'.] walking boots, while the other holds a sketchbook; neither is posed in a yoga position. “A little room around your thoughts” is printed below the photograph. A separate panel names the programme, duration and substantial price. The [pieceful|peaceful|'Piece' means a part. title: Breakfast cereal
text: This sponsored social post for breakfast cereal is filmed by a father during a chaotic morning with his three children. text: A cinema advert for supermarket coffee opens on the empty stage of a community theatre. text: In a podcast advert for speciality coffee, a café owner calls a grower to discuss the coming harvest. title: Everyday watch
text: This radio advert for an everyday watch begins with a young nurse describing how the minutes between patient checks can feel different from the minutes on her journey home. text: A website banner for a luxury watch shows a celebrated architect examining a half-built public [libary|library|Spell 'library' with two r's: li-brar-y.]. text: A sponsored social post for a waterproof coat is filmed during a weekend search for missing dogs after a storm. text: A website banner for gaming headphones depicts an esports team discussing a failed match. text: A billboard for a city bicycle shows a teenage girl teaching her father the safest route to a new community centre. Still, the advert depends on safe cycling [infastructure|infrastructure|Spell 'infrastructure' as infra + structure.] that the bicycle itself cannot provide.

title: Racing bicycle
text: On a billboard for a racing bicycle, the rider is shown after rather than during a race. She leans against a wall, exhausted, while her coach [examine|examines|'Her coach' is one person, so add -s.] the [bikes|bike's|Add 's to show that the chain belongs to the bike.] chain and a teammate brings water. The line “Built for the work between finishes” appears beside the frame's weight and the brand name. The high price is accessible through a QR code, not printed on the main image. Her fatigue and the supporting team [complicates|complicate|'Her fatigue and the supporting team' is plural, so use 'complicate'.] the solitary champion image, although the brand remains positioned as an essential part of [there|their|'There' is a place. 'Their' shows belonging: their collective achievement.] collective achievement.

title: Budget hotel stay
text: A television advert for a budget hotel stay follows two friends visiting a coastal town in winter. Their small room [overlook|overlooks|'Their small room' is singular, so add -s.] a car park, but the receptionist [give|gives|'The receptionist' is one person, so add -s.] them directions to a quieter beach, and they return with windblown hair and takeaway supper. The final card gives the actual room rate, booking conditions and walking time to the station. “Spend the day somewhere new” is the only slogan. By allowing the view to [dissapoint|disappoint|Spell 'disappoint' with one s and a double p.], the advert makes its low price [credibly|credible|After 'makes its low price', use the adjective: credible.]; the receptionist also gets a name and knowledge of the place rather than appearing as anonymous service.

title: Luxury hotel stay
text: A transit poster for a luxury hotel shows a guest looking out across a city from an immaculate room. In the mirror behind her, a housekeeper [adjust|adjusts|'A housekeeper' is one person, so add -s.] the curtains; the reflection is sharp enough to show her expression, but she is unnamed. “A view made for you” appears above a [discrete|discreet|'Discrete' means separate. Quiet and not obvious is 'discreet'.] booking code and the suite's name. The absence of a price and the elevated viewpoint [constructs|construct|'The absence of a price and the viewpoint' is plural, so use 'construct'.] a privileged audience. The composition makes the worker [literary|literally|'Literary' is about literature. 'Literally' means in a real, actual sense.] visible within the luxury being sold, while still placing her at the edge of the guest's experience.

title: Household vacuum cleaner
text: A billboard for a household vacuum cleaner depicts a crowded multigenerational home after a family celebration. A grandfather vacuums [fell|fallen|Use the past participle as an adjective: fallen decorations.] paper decorations while two children collect plates and their aunt [carrys|carries|Change y to -ies: carries.] chairs away. “Everyone can finish the party” appears beside the product, a large price and its warranty. The mess is specific and believable, and no one person is given permanent responsibility for cleaning it. Yet the celebratory context [soften|softens|'The celebratory context' is singular, so add -s.] the routine nature of housework, making the machine seem associated with happy occasions rather than the tasks repeated [everyday|every day|'Everyday' is an adjective. 'Every day' means each day.].

title: Premium robot vacuum
text: In a magazine advert for a premium robot vacuum, a composer works at a piano while the device [travel|travels|'The device' is singular, so add -s.] through her apartment. A second image shows her partner emptying its container and moving a cable out of the way. “More time for the unfinished piece” appears beside the model's name; the price and maintenance requirements [sits|sit|'The price and maintenance requirements' is plural, so use 'sit'.] in a clear panel. The campaign acknowledges that automation [need|needs|'Automation' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: needs.] human attention, although the composer receives the aspirational close-up. Their apartment's broad, uncluttered floor also makes the device's performance look [easily|easier|After 'look', use an adjective: easier.] than it might in a smaller home.

title: Flat-pack sofa
text: An online video for a flat-pack sofa follows three friends moving into a shared apartment. One reads the instructions, another sorts the parts and the third keeps [turn|turning|After 'keeps', use the -ing form: keeps turning.] a panel the wrong way; the edit retains their laughter and an argument about which colour cushion to use. A time-lapse then gives [weigh|way|To 'weigh' is to measure heaviness. 'Give way to' means to be replaced by.] to a quiet final scene in which they sit down together. The price, delivery charge and assembly guide [appears|appear|'The price, charge and guide' is plural, so use 'appear'.] on screen. “Make somewhere to stay” links furniture to a tentative sense of home, without [disguise|disguising|After 'without', use the -ing form: without disguising.] the work of putting it together.

title: Designer sofa
text: A podcast advert for a designer sofa invites listeners into a conversation between an upholsterer and a customer whose daughter uses a wheelchair. They discuss seat depth, fabric that can be cleaned [easy|easily|Use the adverb 'easily' to say how it can be cleaned.] and how everyone will gather in the room. The daughter joins the recording and rejects an impractical arrangement the adults had [agree|agreed|After 'had', use the past participle: had agreed.] on. The host offers a design appointment and names the collection, but gives no price. Her intervention makes her a user with [preferances|preferences|Spell 'preferences' with -ence: prefer + ence.] rather than an abstract accessibility problem; the bespoke service simultaneously [assume|assumes|'The bespoke service' is singular, so add -s.] the family can pay for substantial choice.

title: Shampoo
text: A transit poster for shampoo features a teenage boy with long hair, tying it back before a school science demonstration. A classmate [hold|holds|'A classmate' is one person, so add -s.] the equipment while he checks his notes. “Ready for whatever you are making” is printed beside the bottle, price and a simple claim about gentle washing. The image broadens who can be seen in hair-care advertising without making his appearance a spectacle. The [labratory|laboratory|Spell 'laboratory' with -bor-: la-bor-a-tory.] setting supplies an identity beyond grooming, even though a glossy strand of hair [remain|remains|'A glossy strand of hair' is singular, so add -s.] carefully lit across the centre of the poster. His experiment, rather than his hair, [attract|attracts|The subject is 'his experiment', so use 'attracts'.] the class's attention.

title: Premium skincare serum
text: A television advert for premium skincare serum follows an older woman leading a coastal clean-up. She explains how tides [carries|carry|'Tides' is plural, so use 'carry'.] plastic into a sheltered bay, then returns home and applies the serum after [wash|washing|After 'after', use the -ing form: after washing.] her face. The bottle is shown clearly only in the final seconds, when a caption lists its ingredients, price and the scope of its claims. Her expertise and physical work [structures|structure|'Her expertise and physical work' is plural, so use 'structure'.] the story; her age remains visible. The campaign borrows [morale|moral|'Morale' means the confidence of a group. To do with right and wrong is 'moral'.] weight from environmental action, however, without claiming that the expensive product itself addresses the problem she describes.

title: Mobile data plan
text: A transit poster for a mobile data plan shows a young man translating a voice message for his father at a bus stop. Beside them, the father's reply is printed in two languages: he has already [understand|understood|After 'has', use the past participle: has understood.] the important part. “Keep every conversation open” leads to the allowance, monthly price and roaming limits. The father is neither helpless nor silent; the exchange shows cooperation across languages and generations. Its neat two-line conversation nevertheless [reduce|reduces|'Its neat two-line conversation' is singular, so add -s.] the complexity of maintaining family [tie's|ties|This is a plural, not belonging, so it has no apostrophe: ties.] across countries to a service that can be [purchase|purchased|After 'can be', use the past participle: can be purchased.] by the month.

title: Private tutoring service
text: In a podcast advert for private tutoring, a student reads [an|a|Use 'a' before a consonant sound: a high hourly fee.] paragraph from her history essay and stops when she realises her evidence [do|does|'Her evidence' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: does.] not support the point. Her tutor asks what she actually [want|wants|'She' takes a verb with -s: wants.] to argue; we hear her revise the sentence aloud. The host then gives qualifications, session length and a high hourly fee. “Find the words for your own thinking” closes the segment. The student retains authorship, and the tutoring is presented as questioning rather than answer-giving. The price makes clear that this kind of individual attention remains [uneven|unevenly|Use the adverb 'unevenly' before 'available'.] available.

title: Gym membership
text: A transit poster for a gym membership shows the same class at three moments: entering [uncertain|uncertainly|Use the adverb 'uncertainly' to say how they enter.], resting between exercises and leaving in conversation. A man with a larger body is central in the middle photograph, but no image asks viewers to [comparing|compare|After 'ask someone to', use the base verb: compare.] his shape before and after. “A place to return to” appears beside the monthly price, accessibility details and opening hours. The sequencing [value|values|'The sequencing' is singular, so add -s.] belonging and persistence over visible transformation. Its cheerful group, however, cannot represent everyone who might feel uncomfortable crossing the [threshhold|threshold|Spell 'threshold' with one h in the middle: thresh + old.] for the first time. A trial session is offered without promising that discomfort will vanish.

title: Wellness retreat
text: A sponsored social post for a wellness retreat is narrated by a woman who says she [come|came|She arrived in the past, so use 'came'.] because she needed time to make a difficult decision. We see her walking, writing a letter and speaking briefly with a [councillor|counsellor|A 'councillor' is an elected member of a council. Someone who gives advice is a 'counsellor'.], but the decision itself remains private. The caption lists the [retreats|retreat's|Add 's to show that the activities belong to the retreat.] activities, credentials, dates and substantial cost. “Leave with a little more room” promises no instant cure. Her refusal to [disclosing|disclose|After 'refusal to', use the base verb: disclose.] the outcome gives her control over the story, although the campaign still turns a private period of uncertainty into an [apealing|appealing|Spell 'appealing' with a double p.] destination.

title: Children’s board game
text: A website banner for a children's board game shows a brother and sister arguing about the rules while their aunt waits for [they|them|After 'for', use 'them'.] to settle it. When the cursor moves, the banner reveals each child's proposed solution and the game's actual rule. “Someone always sees another move” links to the age range, playing time and price. Their disagreement is an intellectual part of the play, not a problem [solving|solved|The problem would be solved by an adult, so use the past participle.] by an adult. The interactive format [invite|invites|'The interactive format' is singular, so add -s.] viewers to choose a side, giving the children distinct arguments rather than using their smiles as [prove|proof|'Prove' is a verb. The noun is 'proof'.] of family happiness.

title: Collectable toy set
text: A radio advert for a collectable toy set takes the form of an interview with a child who has [invent|invented|After 'has', use the past participle: has invented.] a story for the figures. She describes a scientist, a pilot and a mechanic escaping a collapsing city, but insists that the mechanic should [decides|decide|After 'should', use the base verb: decide.] where they go. Sound effects briefly [brings|bring|'Sound effects' is plural, so use 'bring'.] her plot to life. A narrator names the figures and gives each separate price. The child's [imaginary|imaginative|'Imaginary' means not real. Full of ideas is 'imaginative'.] authority makes the toys seem open-ended, while the elaborate adventure encourages listeners to [picturing|picture|After 'encourage someone to', use the base verb: picture.] a complete set rather than one affordable purchase.

title: Streaming subscription
text: This television advert for a streaming subscription follows an older woman choosing a documentary about a place where she once [live|lived|She lived there in the past, so use 'lived'.]. Her grandson [assume|assumes|'Her grandson' is one person, so add -s.] she wants a nostalgic programme, but she pauses to challenge the film's account of a local protest she remembers [different|differently|Use the adverb 'differently' to say how she remembers it.]. The screen then shows them searching for another source together. “A story can start a conversation” appears with the subscription price and trial terms. Her memory becomes knowledge rather than a sentimental reaction, although the platform still positions [it's|its|'It's' means 'it is'. 'Its' shows belonging: its catalogue.] catalogue as the convenient starting point for that exchange.

title: Premium bank account
text: A magazine advert for a premium bank account depicts a woman reviewing documents in a railway lounge while her teenage son [read|reads|'Her teenage son' is one person, so add -s.] beside her. A caption identifies her as the founder of a small export [buisness|business|Spell 'business' with -usi-: bus-i-ness.], and the benefits panel [list|lists|'The benefits panel' is singular, so add -s.] international payments, travel support, eligibility rules and the monthly fee. “Work crosses borders. So can your plans” appears in restrained type. Her professional choices are specific, yet the comfortable lounge and seamless journey [compresses|compress|'The lounge and journey' is plural, so use 'compress'.] the difficulties of [run|running|After 'the difficulties of', use the -ing form: of running.] a business across countries into an image of composure available through financial privilege.
